item.name: Overshield

Overshield is most commonly at 50%, though certain enemies have a different Overshield value. To view the Overshield Percentage (How much of their HP is converted to Overshield), check the Enemy Index page or in-game. Abilities that tell the player enemy info, like Slime (King)​'s Great Sage ability, also list Overshield Percentage.
item.cardSummary: Overshield changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect.

item.name: Depleted
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: There is no counter to Depleted. When Depleted appears in a stage, players must try to avoid hitting the enemy with their Meter units, or resort to omitting Meter units from their team.
item.cardSummary: Depleted changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Blinded
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Nature and Unknown are naturally immune to Blinded, since Nature nullifies Range debuffs and Unknown is immune to all. Additionally, all Cleansers can cleanse applications of Blinded, and protectors can protect in the same way. Because of Blinded's on-hit application (one tick per hit), certain cleansers may waste their cleansing ability on a single tick of Blinded before subsequent ticks are applied.
item.cardSummary: Blinded changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Resilient
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Nullify is the main counter for Resilient, as resorting to units that have smaller AOEs can prove detrimental to the match as a whole. However, since Nullify is an effect, enemies with Immunity would be unaffected. As such, the next best counter is using the Gon familiar.
item.cardSummary: Resilient changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Sturdy
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Nature and Water units not only bypass Sturdy's Damage reduction, but receive +40% Damage dealt to their attacks. Since Sturdy works through Damage reduction, Nullify can disable the enemy's Damage reduction, and Bypassers who can bypass Damage reduction are effective as well.
item.cardSummary: Sturdy changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Challenger
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Since Challenger functions purely through summons, there is no inherent counter; normal summons will always fail to damage Challenger enemies, and Elite Summons will always be reduced.
item.cardSummary: Challenger changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Energy Drain
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Spark and Unknown are naturally immune to Energy Drain, since Spark nullifies Damage debuffs and Unknown is immune to all. Additionally, all Cleansers can cleanse applications of Energy Drain, and protectors can protect in the same way. Because of Energy Drain's on-hit application (one tick per hit), certain cleansers may waste their cleansing ability on a single tick of Energy Drain before subsequent ticks are applied.
item.cardSummary: Energy Drain changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Absorption
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Since Absorption functions purely through summons, there is no inherent counter; normal summons will always heal Absorption enemies.
item.cardSummary: Absorption changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Armored
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Nullify is the main counter for Armored, but in many stages where Armored is present, players may want to opt for spamming placements of cheap RareRare units with high placement counts (Jon, for example) due to the cost-effectiveness and universal application of the strategy. Since Armored works through damage reduction, Bypassers who can bypass Damage reduction are effective as well.
item.cardSummary: Armored changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Overshield
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: World Destroyer, World Destroyer (Old) are the main counters for Overshield, as they can completely remove it on-hit. Since Overshield works through damage reduction, Nullify can disable the enemy's Damage reduction, and Bypassers who can bypass damage reduction are effective as well.
item.cardSummary: Overshield changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Fast
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: The best counters for Fast are any Crowd Control effects, with movement stoppers ( Freeze, Stun) being the most effective, followed by Slow, and finally Repulse, since it always repulses by a set distance, independent of Movespeed.
item.cardSummary: Fast changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Regen
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Rupture is the main counter for Regen, as it disables innate regeneration. Bleed is the next best option, as it disables innate regeneration for its duration.
item.cardSummary: Regen changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Shielded
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Tuji (Sorcerer Killer) is the best counter for Shielded, as it completely deletes Shielded on-hit, but due to this unit not having any other uses, it is more optimal to bring a Full AOE multi-hit unit to deplete the shields naturally.
item.cardSummary: Shielded changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Thrice
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: The best counter for Thrice is Full AOE, since the extra spawns won't hinder your units' attacking power on other enemies. Multi-hit units aren't as effective, due to the brief invincibility the copies gain after spawning. Additionally, one can use special bypassers, like Divalo (Requiem), to disable on-death mechanics.
item.cardSummary: Thrice changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Dodge
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Nullify is the best counter for Dodge, as it allows every unit on the player's roster to attack enemies freely. Units that can bypass dodge chance are also viable.
item.cardSummary: Dodge changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.

item.name: Revitalize
item.effect: Applies an enemy mechanic that needs a specific counter.
item.counter: Revitalize can be countered by Bleed, Rupture and Nullify (has to be applied to the enemy that is being killed, not the one being healed). If an enemy with this modifier dies, and they are not under the aforementioned effects, they will hear nearby enemies, regardless of the effects applied to the enemies healed.
item.cardSummary: Revitalize changes a stage or enemy rule, so plan around its listed effect and counter.
